info.title: Kodi JSON-RPC API
info.description: Kodi's JSON-RPC 2.0 API. All methods are served from a single endpoint over HTTP POST and over WebSocket/TCP. Server-initiated notifications are only delivered over WebSocket/TCP and are documented separately in asyncapi.json.

methods.name: Player.SetGeometry
methods.summary: Change the room geometry in force partway through a title, for a system driving a motorised room. Takes effect on the next frame and announces Player.OnContentGeometryChange carrying what Kodi actually did, which is not necessarily what was asked for. A stated raster reaches the layout by the same path the corresponding setting does, so the interface re-selects the layout it holds for the new shape - a change no other field here causes. Everything stated here reverts when playback ends, so an instruction given for one title cannot leave the room in a shape nothing on screen explains. Equivalent to the geometry option of Player.Open, which covers the play-time case without a second call.

methods.name: Player.GetGeometry
methods.summary: The room geometry in force. Reports what was stated for this playback separately from what is actually in effect, because the two differ wherever nothing was stated and the viewer's setting is standing in. An automation that reconnects partway through a title needs both: what it previously asked for, and what the room is doing now.

stated.description: What was stated for this playback. Zero, and null for osdPlacement, mean nothing was stated and the setting applies.

raster.description: The raster in force, whether it came from an override or from the setting. Zero means the same as the display.

osdPlacement.description: The OSD placement in force, from whichever of the two stated it.

screen.description: Where the instruction actually put the picture. Absent while nothing is drawn, which is the same moment the rectangle in contentRect is absent and for the same reason.

params.description: A musicdb://artists/ or musicdb://albums/ path, for "view". Its filter options select the items; an artistId or albumId option and the item in the path are ignored, since the view is the listing. An albums path leaves singles out unless it carries show_singles=true

methods.name: VideoLibrary.RefreshContentGeometry
methods.summary: Measure the content geometry of the file behind the given item again, replacing whatever is stored for it. Unlike the background sweep this does not ask whether the work is needed, so it is the only way to revisit a file that was measured successfully and got the wrong answer. Fails when content geometry detection is disabled, rather than reporting success for work it did not do

file.description: Path to the file itself. Content geometry is stored per file, so this is the only form that can name one version of a movie that has several

params.name: thorough
params.description: Sample far more densely than the setting asks for. A sequence shot in another ratio can sit entirely between two ordinary sample points, which is how a title cut in three ratios is recorded as having one shape; at this density it cannot. Costs roughly a second per point, so it is meant for one title at a time rather than for a library.

methods.name: GUI.TakeScreenshot
methods.summary: Takes a screenshot into the configured screenshot folder and answers with the files it wrote. Waits for the capture to be encoded, so every file it names is complete when the response arrives. Pass a returned path to Files.PrepareDownload to fetch the image. Answers Unavailable when no screenshot folder is configured.

methods.name: GUI.SetScreenAlignment
methods.summary: Show or hide the screen alignment frames, and state which aspect ratios are drawn. The frames are drawn at the true shape and at the full size of the display, ignoring the raster, the overscan calibration and the interface's proportions, because they exist to be aligned to rather than corrected. Intended for programming motorised masking or lens memory presets with nobody at the keyboard: state one ratio, read back what is on screen, programme the preset against it, then move to the next. Session state only - nothing here is written to disk, and neither the set nor the tool survives a restart.

params.name: show
params.description: Whether the frames are on screen. Omitted leaves that as it is, so a set can be stated before the tool is shown, or changed while it is up

params.name: ratios
params.description: The ratios whose frames are drawn, replacing whatever was drawn before. A ratio the vocabulary does not hold is dropped rather than approximated: an installer naming 2.40 and being shown 2.35 would programme the wrong mask position. An empty array draws no frames

schema.description: The state in force, which is what the answer to GUI.GetScreenAlignment would be

Pixel aspect ratio where 1.0 means square pixel
Vertical shift 1.0 means shift to bottom
Flag to enable nonlinear stretch

Player.Geometry.description: What a system driving the room has told Kodi to do for this playback, overriding the corresponding settings. Every field is independent: state only the ones you are driving and the viewer's own choices stand for the rest. An override lasts for this playback only and reverts when it ends. A field omitted, or given as null, is left exactly as it is - so an automation moving the lens need not restate an OSD placement it set earlier. To withdraw a single override without ending playback, give zero for a ratio or "setting" for the placement.

raster.description: The aspect ratio of the area Kodi may operate in. This is the whole of the lens control: nothing Kodi draws ever exceeds the raster, so a motorised room does not opt out of that constraint, it moves it. Both choices for a given title are legitimate and the cost is yours to weigh - a 16:9 title in a 1.78 raster fills the display and the lens zooms in, while the same title in a 2.40 raster is pillarboxed and costs resolution because the lens is zoomed out. Zero means the same as the display.

osdPlacement.description: Whether the interface is laid out against the whole raster or against the picture as it was actually drawn. "setting" withdraws the override and returns this to the viewer's own choice, which is what zero does for the two ratios.

maintain.description: Render this title into the area of the raster with this ratio, so that the picture and the lens memory about to be selected correspond. This is a rendering target, not a claim about the content: a 2.35 film maintained at 1.78 is a valid instruction, and it neither reads nor disturbs any aspect ratio declared for the file. The target nests inside the raster rather than replacing it, so the picture cannot be pushed off the screen. Content wider than the maintained ratio is letterboxed within the target and content taller is pillarboxed within it; content taller than the maintained ratio is unaffected, because it binds on a height the target already has. Zero maintains nothing.

Player.ScreenGeometry.description: Where Kodi actually put the picture, in screen pixels. This is what was done rather than what the content is: a raster and a maintained ratio together decide the rectangle, and neither of those ratios says where the picture landed. Present only while something is drawn.

picture.description: The content on the screen. Black bars coded into the video are outside it, as are the bars Kodi itself is showing around it - this is the lit rectangle, which is what a mask is driven to.

raster.description: The area Kodi is operating in, which the picture is contained by and never exceeds. This is what a lens is driven to, and it is not the picture whenever the content is narrower than the room.

language.description: BCP 47 language tag (e.g. en, en-AU), empty when the stream declares none, und where it declares one that names no language

Video.ContentRect.description: The picture within the frame, after pixel aspect correction. Black bars coded into the video are outside it. The rectangle is absent when there is no frame behind it, which is the case while nothing is playing and Kodi is reporting the shape it rests at; aspect, label and name are always present, and are what a consumer acting on the shape rather than on the pixels should read.

x.description: Absent when there is no frame behind the rectangle, along with the five below - which is the case while nothing is playing and Kodi is reporting the shape it rests at. A library row carries no rectangle at all until its file is measured, so it is never the shape this describes.

frameWidth.description: The whole frame, in the same space, which the rectangle is contained by

aspect.description: The ratio the content was shot at

label.description: Kodi's name for that ratio, empty when it corresponds to none

name.description: What that ratio is called, empty when it has no established name. Served beside label rather than instead of it, and never translated, so it can be compared against.

varies.description: The title changes shape partway through, so one rectangle cannot describe all of it

stale.description: Measured by a superseded detector, and served rather than discarded

rejected.description: A measurement existed and the plausibility gate refused it, so the frame is being served instead. The only thing that tells that apart from never having measured at all, which is otherwise identical: both report source container and both serve the frame. Which of the two it is decides whether the answer is to measure the file or to look at why detection failed on it.

source.description: container means nothing is known and the frame is the answer

sections.description: Every geometry the title was measured in, dominant first, in the same space and frame as the rectangle above. Present whatever decided the rectangle: a declared ratio pins the answer without erasing what was measured, and a measurement the plausibility gate refused is still what detection saw. Empty when nothing was measured, and when the answer is a live reading on a file no stored measurement retained the shapes of. This is what varies can be acted on with.

data.description: The request could not be parsed as JSON.
The request parsed as JSON but is not a well-formed JSON-RPC 2.0 request object.
The requested method does not exist, the client lacks the permission to see it, or it is not available over the transport the request arrived on.
The given parameters do not validate against the schema of the method. The "data" member names the offending parameter and the constraint it failed.
The method failed for a reason that no other status describes.
The method was called correctly but the operation it requested did not succeed. Its code sits one below the -32099..-32000 range JSON-RPC 2.0 reserves for server errors.
The client does not hold every permission the method requires.
The requested item does not exist.
The requested item exists but cannot be provided at the moment.
What was asked for is locked on this installation: a path outside every source shared for remote access, or a setting level the profile's settings lock keeps.

nothing-playing.description: Nothing is playing, or not the playlist the call named.

not-applicable.description: The call does not apply to what it acts on, such as zooming a video, choosing a subtitle for music or repeating the picture playlist.

tempo-unsupported.description: The player of what is playing cannot change its tempo.

paused.description: The call needs playback that is not paused.

no-such-stream.description: What is playing has no stream at the given index.

unreachable.description: The path cannot be read at the moment, as when its share is offline.

no-such-item.description: Nothing has the given id: no library item, and no PVR channel, channel group, broadcast, timer or recording.

no-such-source.description: The directory lies inside no source of the library.

not-in-library.description: The library holds nothing under the directory.

no-such-addon.description: No add-on has the given id, or none that is enabled where the call needs one.

no-such-path.description: Nothing exists at the given path.

outside-sources.description: The path lies outside every source shared for remote access.

not-a-file.description: The path names a directory, not a file.

no-such-setting.description: No setting has the given id.

setting-disabled.description: The setting is disabled by the settings it depends on, so it cannot change now.

change-declined.description: Kodi declined the change, as when a new display mode is not kept or a required add-on would be disabled.

level-locked.description: The profile's settings lock keeps the setting level.

pvr-not-started.description: PVR is off, or has not finished starting.

backend-refused.description: The PVR add-on refused the request or failed to carry it out.

playback-refused.description: Playback did not start, as when a parental lock is not unlocked or a prompt is cancelled.

feature-disabled.description: A setting on this installation turns the feature off.

capture-failed.description: The frame did not arrive, or the screenshot could not be written.

delete-failed.description: The file could not be deleted.

not-supported.description: The system cannot do it, or its power settings do not allow it.

database-not-open.description: Kodi has not opened that database, because it is still starting or opening it failed.

measure-failed.description: The file could not be read or decoded to measure.

party-mode-elsewhere.description: Party mode is running on the other playlist.

timer-exists.description: A timer already exists for the broadcast.

not-playable.description: The item cannot go in the playlist, or holds nothing it can play.
